defects.justification: Routing for POST /imports and GET /imports/{id} performs no authentication, so any network client can upload a CSV that overwrites every field of existing customer records by email (upsert), i.e. unauthenticated mass modification of the customer database.

Each import decodes the whole upload to a String and then materialises every record as Row objects with List copies before processing; a 20 MB file of tiny rows becomes millions of objects (many times the upload size), and up to 10 queued uploads plus 8 in-flight request bodies are held at once, so the README's 'bounded by 20 MB' memory claim understates real usage.

The JDK HttpServer runs on a fixed 8-thread pool (line 51) with no read/idle timeout while each upload of up to 20 MB is read synchronously; eight slow-upload clients block all requests, including status polling.
URLDecoder.decode throws IllegalArgumentException on a malformed percent escape in the status query string (e.g. ?errorsLimit=%zz); it is not caught in status() and becomes a 500 instead of a 400.
